object_description: sculptural new school volume set into a reinterpreted sequence of squares, sunk at its entrance
geometry_property: group rooms in a middle layer at the front
doubled pavilion figure created by demolition
design_condition: the scheme demolishes one listed pavilion to reinterpret the outdoor space as a coherent sequence of squares, with the new building as its sculptural highlight and a narrowing that extends the view to the nearby forest

positive: The demolition reveals a surprising exterior spatial potential
The value of the doubled pavilion building for zoning the outdoor spaces is appreciated
From an urban planning perspective the proposal is certainly impressive
With a clear gesture the outdoor space is reinterpreted as a coherent dramaturgy
The new school building is the sculptural highlight of this sequence
A cleverly placed narrowing extends the view beyond the sports field to the forest and gives a poetic spatial conclusion
Existing outdoor spaces around the old buildings are largely retained
Gymnasium courtyard and new building are directly integrated into the sequence of squares, adding value for the neighbourhood
The partial greening of the gymnasium courtyard is logical and relates the recreation area well to its surroundings
It also partially conceals the unattractive front of the building
The clear arrangement of uses along the rhythmic outdoor space is convincing
Day school and gymnasium mediate meaningfully between the pavilions and the new building
The new building impresses with the clarity of its organisation
The ground floor offers a spacious reception and a representative combination of collective uses
The upper floors offer sufficient, centrally lit access space
The group rooms in the middle layer at the front allow very flexible use
Interventions in the existing buildings remain minimal apart from the demolition
The concept is compliant with the energy standard together with the roof photovoltaics
A very valuable contribution to the discussion about worthiness of protection
negative: Demolishing the listed pavilion runs contrary to the formulated specifications and was controversially discussed
Exposing the not very representative gymnasium facade opposite the very large square figure is criticised
The lowered entrance, which sinks into the ground unlike the existing buildings, remains incomprehensible
The reorganisation of the primary school interior with the proposed group rooms is not entirely convincing
The architectural expression remains correct but not very context-specific
It is clearly inferior to the radical situational solution in terms of creating identity
Additional measures in insulation perimeter and shading are needed for the energy standard
Reusing the existing gas heating leads to extended intervention in the existing building
The demolition and additional new construction area increase grey energy and costs
Construction costs are higher due to the additional new construction area
It is questionable whether the demolition delivers corresponding added value
Doubts arise whether the very large, almost oversized exterior space does justice to the scale of the complex
